claim_summary: The work trains LLMs for open-ended event forecasting using a curated news-derived dataset, calibrated outcome rewards, and date-bounded news retrieval.

claim_evidence.quote: In this work, we train language models to make predictions on open-ended forecasting questions.

modules.name: Open-ended forecasting model training
modules.scope_reason: R2 places GRPO model updates on the LLM side; no Harness layer applies.

evidence.quote: We train the Qwen3-8B thinking model with GRPO on OpenForesight

modules.name: OpenForesight training dataset
modules.scope_reason: R2 treats data specifically constructed to train the model as LLM-side training data.
rubric_path: R1:contributed dataset built for the LLM

evidence.quote: to create OpenForesight, a dataset of ∼ 50,000 open-ended forecasting questions for training.

modules.name: Resolution-date-bounded static news retrieval
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because retrieval is bounded by each forecasting question's resolution date to construct its admissible evidence; the task-specific cutoff must be redesigned when forecast resolution semantics change.

evidence.quote: To prevent leakage issues (Paleka et al., 2025a), we use our offline CCNews corpus, and only use articles up to one month before the question’s resolution date.

temporal_validity.quote: We take extensive measures to avoid the leakage of future information during training and evaluation.

task_performance.quote: RL training on OpenForesight makes the predictions of our specialized 8B model competitive with much larger proprietary models in both accuracy and calibration.

notes: Open-ended forecasting concerns discrete future world events rather than numerical time-series forecasting; the source explicitly describes training language models to predict future events.
